## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

Exact first variations governed by one linear equation superpose, with compatible initial data; they have no intrinsic interaction residual. For finite perturbations, first define a shared baseline and the individual interventions before subtracting their state differences. Otherwise the displayed residual is ambiguous and may count the baseline or initial displacement repeatedly.

A finite-response residual can contain higher-order state/input coupling. In a comparison with numerical or measured data it may also contain solver, parameter, noise and model errors. Taylor Hessians in a coordinate chart are not automatically Riemannian curvature. A computed residual is a discrepancy; a certified error bound additionally requires declared norms, smoothness and propagation estimates. See [the canonical residual construction](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-4-residuals-curvature.html).

## 1. Decomposition with Residuals

$$
\delta x(t_1)
= \sum_i \delta x_i(t_1) + r.
$$

The residual term $r$ captures higher-order curvature effects.

## 2. Meaning of Residuals

Residuals quantify nonlinear coupling, not modeling error.

## 3. Validity Regime

Residual magnitude provides a natural error bound for attribution.

:::
